item.title: Jason Derulo Testifies at ‘Savage Love’ Trial, Says Guitarist Suing Him ‘Created Absolutely Nothing’
item.description:
[Intro music plays, followed by the host]
Host: Welcome to this special report. Jason Derulo took the stand in a Los Angeles federal courtroom last Thursday, denying claims that a session musician deserves writing and production royalties for his hit song "Savage Love". Let's dive into the details.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: The song, which reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100, was a viral TikTok hit in 2020, and later got a remix featuring BTS. The plaintiff, Matthew Spatola, claims he contributed key creative elements to the instrumentals, but was cut out of the lucrative royalties. Derulo, however, testified that Spatola simply played the guitar and bass parts he was given, and didn't create anything original.
[Music transitions to a short clip of "Savage Love"]
Host: Derulo stated that he composes his own instrumentals and chooses his collaborators carefully. He claims he had never met Spatola before the musician came to his home studio for two sessions in April 2020. Derulo also mentioned that Spatola was paid a $2,000 fee for his work, but they never signed a formal work-for-hire agreement, which would have confirmed that Spatola didn't have authorship rights.
[Music returns to the soft background tune]
Host: The absence of this agreement is at the heart of the dispute. Spatola argues that it proves he deserves creative credits, while Derulo disagrees. The jury will now decide which version of events is true. Deliberations are set to begin next week. We'll be following this story and bringing you updates as more information becomes available.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for now. Thanks for tuning in to this special report. Join us next time for more news and updates from the world of entertainment.
